newsitem.title: POLAND: National Express to keep Polish subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: National Express to keep Polish subsidiary.

text.p: British coach and rail group National Express will keep its Polish subsidiary Polski Express going despite losses made by the firm, the Polish firm's director said on Thursday.
"National Express is not closing down the Polish Express firm," Chris Watts told a news conference.

Watts denied reports by the Polish media that the National Express would sell its Polish unit or dismantle the company and said they contributed to the company's recent loss of about 10 percent of passangers.
Before the loss the company carried up to 70,000 passengers a month.

Watts said the company had a net loss of 0.5 million pounds in the first half of 1996 but said the second half of the year might prove better because of an increase in number of passengers. He did not reveal the 1996 estimated earnings.
Polski Express, set up in 1994 is operating on five main routes in Poland with 23 coaches.
